modifications: Unrigged Tripo export in 19 parts (389,818 triangles, three 2048 px textures: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material), standing on four feet facing -X. Welded across UV seams and the seams between parts (403 edges split at T-junctions, 35 pinholes filled), decimated as one mesh with the head keeping relatively more detail, and split back into its 19 parts: 38,000 triangles, closed (remake/tools/blender-decimate.py ... parts, Blender 5.2, the script as rewritten on branch gramedla, d919175; kept as source/stegosaurus-parts.glb). Baked by remake/tools/bake/bake-quadruped.js (run with bake-character.mjs): turned to face +X, scaled to 7 m long (3.74 m high), stood on the ground with the root midway between the feet, the parts told apart by position (body, head and neck, four legs; 11 plates and the two pairs of tail spikes ride rigidly on the bone under their base), rigged with 21 bones, welded into one closed, consistently wound skin (4 zero-area slivers dropped) whose seams share their weights, three clips authored in code (quadruped-clips.js), merged into one skinned mesh with one matte single-sided material (roughness 0.62, no metalness, normal map at 0.5), base colour (no recolour) and normal map as 1024 px JPEG, the metal/roughness map dropped.
rig: Our bake tool for quadrupeds. Bones: root, Hips, Spine, Chest, Neck, Neck2, Head, Tail1-Tail6, and for each leg one rigid bone hanging from the root with the foot below it, named as the engine's footing plants them: BackLeg.L/R, BackFoot.L/R, FrontLeg.L/R, FrontFoot.L/R; identity rest rotations. A leg swings from a pivot on its axis at half the height (1.87 m); the skin blends from the leg into the body between the top of the leg part and the pivot, and the body around it follows as a harmonic field. Clips: idle 4.0 s; walk 2.43 s, 2.21 m a cycle (0.91 m/s; four beats in lateral sequence, a foot down 55 % of the cycle, landing flat and sweeping back at exactly that speed, passing under its pivot; the hips and shoulders ride as high as their planted legs reach); kink 2.4 s (a friendly nod: the chin lifts a little, the head dips 25 degrees and then less, and comes back). The feet stay planted in idle and kink; in a scene the engine's footing plants them in walks, starts, stops and turns on the spot.
pose: Rest pose on four feet, head, back and tail level, two staggered rows of plates and four tail spikes; faces -X; 0.98 units long, 0.52 high.
sourceTextures: three 2048 px JPEG: base colour, metal/roughness, normal map; one double-sided material
lookCheck: qa/remake/shots/kambedla-look/ (grunnur review shots with her added at 7 m beside Mosi at 8.5 m and Egill at 1.1 m: lineup, three, face, hero, behind, walk, kink), qa/remake/shots/kambedla-r1/ (rig, weights, walk, nod and look turns, back faces in magenta) and qa/remake/shots/stego-look/ (the source as received).
budget: GPU at the tablet preset, 1280x800 on the Iris Xe laptop, __benchmark medians, runs with and without her interleaved in one page load (six rounds each), six loads per shot (grunnur review shots with her staged at 7 m beside Mosi and Egill, and the scene at t=24 with her in view): she adds 0.3 to 1.6 ms, median about 0.8 (her face filling the frame about 1.1), nearly all of it the lit material where she covers the frame; 30k instead of 38k triangles, no shadow, no normal map or drawing the characters first each change it by 0.3 ms or less. Whole frames with her 5.5 to 8.2 ms, over 6 ms in most loads; the same frames without her 4.6 to 7.1 ms, about 1 ms slower than the scene measured the same morning (the laptop was warm after long benchmark runs; other sessions shared the GPU). Triangles, shadow pass included: 277k to 305k (201k to 229k without her); 38 to 49 draw calls.
notes: Violet body, plum back, lilac-cream belly, lilac plates and ivory spikes, as in the concept and STYLE.md section 3 (the row takes its values from this model). Friendly face, closed smile, no teeth. Real adult size: 7 m from nose to tail tip.
